auto_sync (release-3.1): "To enable automatic sync when the live cluster's state deviates from the state defined in Git" (selfHeal); "the sync will be attempted again after self-heal timeout (5 seconds by default)". Script 53-57: scale to 4, loop up to 120 s for 2, no commit, no app_refresh. Output line 15: "shortly after: 2 replicas, Synced".

Architecture (release-3.1): the application controller "continuously monitors running applications and compares the current, live state against the desired target state" and "detects OutOfSync application state". auto_sync: timeout.reconciliation "defaults to 120s with added jitter of 60s for a maximum period of 3 minutes". Supports "rereads Git every few minutes" and continuous comparison.

Sync Options (release-3.1): "Currently, when syncing using auto sync Argo CD applies every object in the application." "Turning on the selective sync option will sync only out-of-sync resources." The scaled api Deployment is itself out of sync (output line 3: OutOfSync), so a selective sync would also reset it to 2. The default is true, but the lesson's 'can be set to apply only the differing objects ... So' implies the setting would have kept 4 replicas; it would not.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: A sync applies the objects of the Application that differ from Git, and the scaled api is one of them, whichever commit started the sync. So the unrelated commit set the api back to the 2 replicas Git declares.

claim_verdicts.evidence: auto_sync (release-3.1): "automated sync will not delete resources when Argo CD detects the resource is no longer defined in Git." Sync Options: "The app will be out of sync if Argo CD expects a resource to be pruned." Output lines 7-8: "configmap/prune-demo", "ConfigMap/prune-demo: requiresPruning=true" after app_wait OutOfSync at the removal commit (script line 40).

auto_sync (release-3.1): "automated sync will not delete resources when Argo CD detects the resource is no longer defined in Git" supports the outcome. But 'Not even the automated sync for that commit' asserts such a sync runs; the repo's own script line 39 says "(No sync starts for this commit: all that differs is an object to prune.)" and the docs do not say either way. Execution (OutOfSync, requiresPruning=true) cannot tell the two apart. Drop the dependence.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Without `prune: true`, the object keeps running, marked as requiring pruning: while `prune` is off, no automated sync deletes it. With prune on, the automated sync of that commit deletes the object.

claim_verdicts.evidence: auto_sync (release-3.1): "Automated sync will only attempt one synchronization per unique combination of commit SHA1 and application parameters. If the most recent successful sync in the history was already performed against the same commit-SHA and parameters, a second sync will not be attempted, unless selfHeal flag is set to true." The last successful sync was the 'Add' commit; the 'Remove' commit was never synced, so once prune is on automated sync is due for it with or without selfHeal. Crediting self-heal misattributes the trigger.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: No commit is pushed: the Application is still `OutOfSync` at the removal commit, which has not been synced yet. Now that `prune` is on, automated sync syncs that commit, and the sync deletes the ConfigMap.

issues.text: Misattributes the prune sync to self-heal (claim 8). Per auto_sync docs, automated sync attempts one sync per commit SHA; the removal commit was never synced, so once prune is on a sync is due regardless of selfHeal. The sentence teaches that self-heal is what made the deletion happen; the junior review already read it that way ('that commit's sync already ran').
issues.quote: the Application is still `OutOfSync` because of `prune-demo`, and with self-heal on that difference is enough to start a sync, which now deletes the ConfigMap
issues.fix: Replace with: "No commit is pushed: the Application is still `OutOfSync` at the removal commit, which has not been synced yet. Now that `prune` is on, automated sync syncs that commit, and the sync deletes the ConfigMap." Update claim 8 text accordingly.

issues.text: Non-sequitur (claim 5). Selective sync 'will sync only out-of-sync resources', and the scaled api is out of sync, so with that setting the unrelated commit would still reset it to 2. Mentioning the setting and then 'So' implies the setting would have kept 4. Same framing in s5 ('applies the whole folder, which is why the api is back to 2'), s6 item 3 and summary line 3 ('which by default applies the whole folder').
issues.quote: Argo CD can be set to apply only the differing objects, but Đơn Hàng does not use that setting. So the unrelated commit set the api back to the 2 replicas Git declares.
issues.fix: Delete the clause about the setting. Write: "A sync applies every object of the Application, not only the files the commit changed, and the scaled api differs from Git. So the unrelated commit set the api back to the 2 replicas Git declares." In s6 item 3 and summary 3 drop 'by default'.

issues.text: Beyond depth_notes: the lesson introduces a selective-sync setting (ApplyOutOfSyncOnly) the outline does not list; depth_notes only asks that any commit's sync applies the whole folder and restores replicas.

issues.text: requiresPruning is set whenever a tracked live object has no manifest in Git, not only while prune is off; with prune on it is simply deleted at the next sync. 'while prune is off' ties the mark to the setting.
issues.quote: the mark Argo CD puts on such an object while prune is off
issues.fix: Write: "Requires pruning — the mark Argo CD puts on an object of the Application whose manifest left Git; while prune is off, the object keeps running and the Application is `OutOfSync` because of it."
